about: Where each coding agent keeps its extensions (MCP servers, hooks, plugins) and in what format. The guard checks every agent's files, not only those of the agent that called it: an agent running under Claude Code that edits ~/.codex/config.toml or .cursor/mcp.json plants an extension in that other agent. Only the formats are data here; guard/agent_config.py interprets them. To add an agent, write one entry in this file and put the evidence you checked in source (verified false = not confirmed against official docs). files = path endings (user and project locations), format = json|toml, servers/hooks/enabled = key paths inside the document (joined with '.', '*' = any key), plugin_dirs = folders where plugins are installed ({config} = the agent's config folder, {market}, {name}; a trailing '*' is a version folder). plugin_manifest = the definition file inside a plugin folder. marketplaces = local marketplace copies (known = registry list, dirs = copy folders, catalogue = list file inside a copy). vars = variables the agent fills in hook and MCP commands (plugin_root, project_dir).

claude-code.source: a local installation (2026-10-23) and the repository adapter (guard/adapters/claude_code.py)

codex.source: official docs learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp (read 2026-10-23), the layout of a local ~/.codex/config.toml and plugins/cache, the repository's .codex/hooks.json

gemini-cli.source: a copy of the Gemini CLI settings docs (mcpServers in ~/.gemini/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json); the official page itself could not be read
